messages:
Lara H: quick idea — can we add a small manifest alongside safetensors blobs to enable atomic "hot-swap" + lazy-verify? thinking partial checksum + chunk map so runtime can serve first tokens while background validates the rest.

Ben K: hmm. the runtime already has warmup vs cold path. are you proposing a new on-disk artifact? :thinking_face: 

Lara H: yeah, a tiny .smanifest next to model.safetensors. contains per-shard chunk digests, byte ranges, and an optional 'verify-policy' flag. runtime would read manifest synchronously, map first N chunks, serve, then finish verify async.

Irene: we experimented with a similar pattern for tarball overlays but worried about complexity when shard placement changes. how do we keep manifest compatible with sharding schemes?

Lara H: manifest would reference a content-hash for each shard file (sha256) + a small proto field 'logical_shard_id' so we can match even if filenames differ. also include 'schema_version'.

Matt: can we see a tiny example?

Lara H: sure — very rough: 
```json
{
  "schema": "smanifest-v1",
  "model": "gpt-3.5-like",
  "shards": [
    {"logical_shard": 0, "file": "model-000.safetensors", "offsets": [[0,65536],[65536,131072]], "digest": "sha256:aa..."},
    {"logical_shard": 1, "file": "model-001.safetensors", "offsets": [[0,131072]], "digest": "sha256:bb..."}
  ],
  "verify_policy": "async-continue-on-first-chunk"
}
```

Ben K: a few concerns: 1) how do we handle quantized formats where bytes aren't stable across conversions, 2) risk of serving bad tokens before verify completes, 3) signature/kms for manifests?

Irene: +1 on signatures. if manifest is separate we need to ensure it's covered by the same auth as weights (signed by publisher). otherwise it becomes an attack surface.

Lara H: agree. plan: manifests signed with model-publisher key (detached sig) and runtime verifies signature before trusting 'digest' entries. if sig missing -> fall back to strict sync-verify path.

Alex P: for quantized/converted blobs we can include a 'conversion-fingerprint' metadata field to indicate encoder used. runtime can treat those shards as 'non-verifiable' and force sync-copy+verify.

Matt: operational question: how would we roll this out? we can't change all customers at once. need backwards compatibility.

Lara H: rollout plan: 1) accept manifest if present, but don't require it; 2) add runtime flag --enable-hot-swap-manifest; 3) Canary for 2 weeks on internal models; 4) expose admit/deny in console per model version.

Ben K: sounds reasonable. what about fallback when manifest digest mismatch? immediate failover to fallback model? or continue but mark degraded?

Irene: for safety i'd prefer fail-open only for non-critical infra tests. For prod we should fail closed and trigger fallback model routing. we already have routing policies for degraded variants.

Lara H: suggested policy: if async verify fails for any chunk -> mark shard 'corrupt' and route requests to fallback model variant; if verify still pending after X secs -> continue serving but with 'degraded' telemetry tag so console can alert.

infra-bot: deploy-check: manifest-signing lib updated -> RFC required for key management changes. See https://infra/redwood/keys/manifest-sig (stub).

deploy-bot: canary job queued for runtime+loader with --enable-hot-swap-manifest on small GPU pool. ETA 2 days.

Matt: one more: metrics. we need per-model metrics for manifest-miss, async-verify-latency, chunks-verified/sec, and dropped-shards. also an eval hook to compare outputs pre/post verify to detect silent corruption.

Lara H: added to plan. I'll write RFC follow-up with samples, API surface for manifest reader, and a migration checklist. anyone want to pair on the RFC?

Ben K: I'll review and add the security/KMS bits.

Irene: I'll draft the test harness for corrupt-shard scenarios.

Alex P: can take prototype loader changes.

Lara H: thanks all. created a tiny GH draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pulls/834 (WIP) :rocket:
